team: Solo founder listed: Karthik Ramakrishnan, President and Chief Business Officer, with substantial AI go-to-market and strategy experience. He previously led GTM teams as VP at Element AI, leading AI solutions and strategy for financial institutions and regulators globally (Founder bio: Karthik Ramakrishnan). He is a repeat founder, having co-founded Blu Trumpet (CTO) and Gallop Labs (CEO), and helped set up Deloitte's global product factory and AI offerings (Founder bio: Karthik Ramakrishnan). He authored a widely cited whitepaper on fairness evaluation of AI models and AI enterprise strategy (Founder bio: Karthik Ramakrishnan). Note: the bio describes him as President/CBO, implying other executives (e.g., a CEO) exist who are not listed in the sources — a gap in the founding-team picture. Team size is 14 (YC profile).
product: Armilla AI sells liability insurance for generative AI and AI agents (One-liner). It operates as an MGA and Lloyd's Coverholder dedicated to insuring AI-related risks, positioning itself as the first YC-backed entity of this kind (YC long description). Policies cover both developers and deployers of generative AI and AI agents for performance and liability — spanning errors, hallucinations, incorrect decisions, data leakage and regulatory violations (YC long description). In plain terms, this is an insurance/risk-transfer business for AI systems, not itself an autonomous agent product.
market: The sources indicate the company sits at the intersection of Fintech, Insurance, Artificial Intelligence and Generative AI (YC tags), and claims to be the first YC-backed MGA and Lloyd's Coverholder focused on AI risk (YC long description). No market size, TAM, customer counts, revenue, competitors, or funding figures are provided in the sources — these are unknown and should not be assumed. The implicit why-now is the rise of generative AI and AI agents creating new performance and liability exposures (errors, hallucinations, regulatory violations) that need insuring (YC long description), but the sources give no traction or demand evidence to validate timing.
risks: Thesis mismatch: the thesis targets AI-native autonomous agents that own high-value business workflows, but Armilla is an insurance provider for AI risk, not an agent that autonomously executes a workflow (One-liner; YC long description). The rule-based score reflects this with 0/30 on workflow ownership and 0/15 on autonomy.
